## Production Mainframe Troubleshooting Index (78 Runbooks)
- [Resolving ABEND S0C7 (Data Exception) in COBOL Packed-Decimal (COMP-3) Fields Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/soc7-data-exception-cobol-packed-decimal.html): ABEND S0C7 occurs when an arithmetic statement or NUMERIC test encounters invalid packed-decimal data (such as uninitialized spaces X'4040' or low-values X'0000') in a COMP-3 field without a valid nibble sign (C, D, or F). Fix it using INITIALIZE, defensive NUMERIC checks, and proper compiler options.
- [Debugging ABEND S0C4 (Protection Exception) in COBOL Linkage Section & Pointers Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/soc4-protection-exception-linkage-pointer.html): ABEND S0C4 (0C4) indicates a hardware storage protection violation caused by dereferencing a NULL pointer, exceeding table OCCURS subscript boundaries without bounds checking, or accessing unallocated Linkage Section items. Learn how to parse the PSW, TEA, and CEEDUMP to isolate the invalid memory address.
- [Mastering SB37, SD37, and SE37 Out-of-Space ABENDs in z/OS Sequential & PDS Datasets Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/sb37-sd37-se37-space-abends-jcl.html): Space ABENDs (SB37, SD37, SE37) crash critical overnight batch jobs when datasets exceed volume, extent, or catalog limits. Discover how to configure secondary allocations, RLSE, SMS Dataclasses, and Extended Format attributes to prevent volume exhaustion.
- [Diagnosing ABEND S0C1 (Operation Exception) in CICS & Batch Execution Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/s0c1-operation-exception-cics-load.html): ABEND S0C1 occurs when the mainframe CPU attempts to execute an instruction with an invalid or undefined operation code. Common causes include calling an unlinked dummy subroutine, branching into Working-Storage data, or mismatched AMODE/RMODE compiler parameters.
- [Resolving ASRA ABENDs in IBM CICS TS: Command-Level Debugging & CEDF Analysis Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/asra-abend-cics-debugging-cedf.html): CICS ASRA is the general transaction abend code indicating a program check (S0C4, S0C7, S0C1, etc.) inside an online transaction. Learn how to locate the execution offset in the CICS Transaction Dump, use CEDF and CEBR to inspect storage, and fix transaction failures.
- [Fixing CICS AEY9 ABEND: Transaction & Resource Security Key Check Failures Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/aey9-abend-cics-security-racf.html): CICS ABEND AEY9 occurs when a user or surrogate identity attempts to execute a transaction or access a protected CICS resource (file, program, TS queue) without required RACF, ACF2, or Top Secret authorization. Understand ESM class definitions and command security.
- [Taming Language Environment (LE) User ABEND U4038: CEEDUMP Analysis & TRAP Tuning Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/u4038-le-runtime-abend-troubleshooting.html): User ABEND U4038 occurs when an unhandled condition of severity 2 or greater terminates a Language Environment (LE) enclave. Learn how to decipher the CEEDUMP traceback, inspect condition tokens, and configure runtime options like TERMTHDACT and TRAP.
- [Resolving IMS DB/DC U0777 and U0778 Deadlocks in Fast Path & Full-Function Databases Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/u0778-u0777-ims-dc-deadlock-resolution.html): IMS U0777 and U0778 pseudo-abends occur when two concurrent Message Processing Programs (MPP) or BMP batch jobs deadlock while competing for database segments or Fast Path DEDB control intervals. Learn lock sequence structuring, commit strategies, and lock timeout tuning.
- [Resolving DB2 SQLCODE -911 (Reason 00C90088 / Deadlock) and -904 Resource Unavailable Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/db2-sqlcode-911-904-resource-unavailable-deadlocks.html): DB2 SQLCODE -911 indicates your unit of work was rolled back due to a deadlock (Reason 00C90088) or lock timeout (Reason 00C9008E). SQLCODE -904 indicates an unavailable resource (tablespace locked, thread limit exceeded). Discover root causes and concurrency tuning.
- [DB2 z/OS Query Optimization: Converting Stage 2 (Residual) into Stage 1 (Indexable) Predicates Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/db2-stage-1-vs-stage-2-predicates-tuning.html): In DB2 for z/OS, Stage 1 (sargable) predicates are evaluated inside the Data Manager (DM) at near-hardware speeds, while Stage 2 (residual) predicates require transferring rows to the Relational Data System (RDS), burning massive CPU. Learn how to refactor SQL for Stage 1 execution.
- [How Outdated RUNSTATS Cause Catastrophic Tablespace Scans in DB2 for z/OS Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/db2-runstats-index-clustering-optimizer.html): When RUNSTATS statistics are stale or missing, the DB2 Cost-Based Optimizer makes catastrophic access path choices, selecting full tablespace scans over clustered indexes. Master RUNSTATS parameters, real-time statistics (RTS), and access path stability.
- [Preventing DB2 Lock Escalation: Tuning LOCKSIZE, Isolation Levels, and SKIP LOCKED DATA Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/db2-lock-escalation-isolation-levels.html): When a transaction acquires more locks than DSNZPARM NUMLKTS, DB2 automatically escalates page/row locks to an exclusive tablespace lock, freezing out all concurrent users. Learn how to tune LOCKSIZE, use Isolation CS, and implement SKIP LOCKED DATA for high-throughput queues.

Learn how to inspect element master records, clear orphaned signouts, and cast packages cleanly.
- [Preventing ChangeMan ZMF Component Desynchronization with Automated Cross-Reference (XREF) Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/changeman-zmf-component-recompile-drift.html): In Serena / Micro Focus ChangeMan ZMF, modifying a shared copybook without recompiling all dependent COBOL programs creates silent runtime data corruption. Discover how to configure ChangeMan XREF data collection and audit triggers.
- [Preventing Memory Leaks and TSO/E Exhaustion in High-Volume Enterprise REXX Automation Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/rexx-stem-variable-memory-leak-cleanup.html): REXX stem variables (e.g. RECORD.i) allocate virtual memory dynamically. In long-running automation loops processing millions of records, failing to drop stems causes virtual storage exhaustion and TSO/E ABEND S878. Learn memory management best practices in REXX.
- [Parsing z/OS SMF Type 30 (Job Accounting) and Type 110 (CICS Telemetry) Records with REXX Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/rexx-parsing-smf-records-system-auditing.html): System Management Facilities (SMF) records are the black box of z/OS. Discover how to write high-speed REXX scripts that decode SMF Type 30 (CPU/Job accounting) and Type 110 (CICS transaction metrics) without purchasing expensive third-party reporting tools.
- [Native JSON Parsing and Generation in Enterprise COBOL 6.x for Modern REST Gateways Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/cobol-json-generate-json-parse-zowe-apis.html): Eliminate middleware gateways. Discover how to use Enterprise COBOL 6.x native JSON GENERATE and JSON PARSE statements to consume and emit UTF-8 JSON payloads directly inside z/OS batch and CICS programs.
- [Accelerating Batch SQL by 400%: Implementing DB2 Multi-Row FETCH and Multi-Row INSERT in COBOL Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/db2-multi-row-fetch-insert-batch-tuning.html): Single-row SQL cursors incur CPU cross-memory switching costs on every single row. Learn how to implement DB2 for z/OS Multi-Row FETCH and Multi-Row INSERT in COBOL, reducing batch elapsed times and CPU consumption by up to 70%.
- [Replacing Custom COBOL Extract Programs with High-Performance DFSORT / ICETOOL Control Statements Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/syncsort-dfsort-icetool-batch-reporting.html): Writing full COBOL programs just to filter, reformat, and aggregate sequential files burns developer hours and CPU cycles. Learn how to use DFSORT and ICETOOL operators (SPLICE, SELECT, STATS, DISPLAY) to execute high-speed batch data manipulations directly in JCL.
- [Breaking the 32KB Limit: Transitioning CICS Commareas to Channels and Containers Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/cics-channels-containers-replacing-commarea.html): Traditional CICS communication is restricted by the rigid 32KB DFHCOMMAREA barrier. Discover how to modernize program-to-program and web interfaces using CICS Channels and Containers, supporting multi-megabyte JSON payloads and modular data structures.
- [Decoding the SCRT Report: Identifying 4HRA Spikes and Sub-Capacity Pricing Anomalies Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/sub-capacity-reporting-tool-scrt-optimization.html): IBM Monthly License Charges (MLC) are dictated by your monthly Sub-Capacity Reporting Tool (SCRT) submission. Learn how to parse SCRT CSV logs, identify which LPAR and batch workload caused the peak billing hour, and implement capacity caps.
- [Diagnosing CICS AICA (Runaway Task) and Storage Violations (Subpool Overwrites) Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/cics-storage-violation-aica-runaway-task.html): CICS ABEND AICA halts transactions that loop without yielding CPU control to CICS task dispatcher, while storage violations corrupt transaction work areas. Discover how to inspect the CICS System Dump, identify runaway loops, and configure storage protection keys.
- [Mastering DB2 Package Plan Stability: Avoiding Access Path Regressions During REBIND Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/db2-rebind-stability-package-plan-switching.html): Rebinding DB2 packages after software maintenance or schema changes can cause access path regressions, resulting in sudden 10x query slowdowns. Master DB2 Plan Management (PLANMGMT), APREUSE, and catalog switching to safeguard production workloads.
- [Handling DB2 SQLCODE -305: Null Indicator Variables in COBOL Working-Storage Fix](https://stackmf.com/blog/cobol-null-indicators-db2-host-variables.html): DB2 SQLCODE -305 is raised when a query attempts to retrieve a NULL column value into a COBOL host variable without specifying an accompanying Null Indicator variable. Learn proper indicator syntax and default coalescing.
